notes: 2018_03 (faculty and unclassified staff handbook page) is a policy-library page linking the handbook PDF; no policy text of its own.

Governing documents: the KU FMLA policy, Modified Instructional Duties policy, Interruption of the Probationary Period (Tenure Clock) policy, Sick Leave and Shared Leave policies, and the Kansas Board of Regents Policy Manual ch. II (binding on KU). The 2010 handbook (file 2017-01-19) says it 'is not itself a source of policy'; it is used only for context and agrees with the policies; nothing rests on it alone.

KU has no paid parental or maternity leave in these sources. Pay during a birth comes only from the employee's own accrued sick leave (KBOR: personal illness includes pregnancy, childbirth, adoption and recovery), which must be exhausted during FMLA before leave becomes unpaid. Shared (donated) leave excludes pregnancy and care of a healthy newborn.

Chain, birth parent: FMLA 12 workweeks (parental c1; own serious health condition c2; 12 combined, leave_limits) with own sick leave (c4) used within it → donated shared leave (c5) only after all paid leave is exhausted and only for an extreme or life-threatening condition (not pregnancy itself); modified instructional duties (c7, one semester, discretionary) also available in addition to sick leave; tenure-clock delay (c8/c9).

Chain, non-birth parent: FMLA 12 workweeks (parental c1, or care of a seriously ill legal spouse c3; 12 combined) with own sick leave (c4, family illness or adoption) used within it; modified instructional duties (c7) also available for a primary or co-equal caregiver; tenure-clock delay (c8/c9).
Calendar: KBOR II.A.1.a states two sixteen-week semesters (term_weeks 16); the handbook's older text says 'at least 15 weeks'.

Regents II.C.10.j.ii only permits universities to adopt a tenure extension after FMLA leave; KU's adoption of it is c10. Regents II.C.10.d (sick leave) and II.C.10.i (shared leave) are coded with the KU policies (c4, c5).

Not components: sabbatical leave (advanced study or research), bereavement, jury/civic leave, leave for elective office, professional-development release time, and the discretionary holiday (purposes a parent cannot use for the birth, or not leave for faculty on academic-year appointments).

Documents cited but not saved: KU Family Medical Leave Act (FMLA) Procedures; Family & Medical Leave Act (FMLA) FAQs; HRM FMLA web page (humanresources.ku.edu/family-and-medical-leave); FMLA Poster and DOL Fact Sheets #28A/#28M; University Policy on Leave Without Pay; Voluntary Leave without Pay with Benefits procedure; Leave Advancement Policy; Sick Leave Overview/Chart (academic-year faculty); Sick leave payout page; Shared Leave Guide and request/donation forms; University Support Staff Handbook; K.A.R. 1-9-5; University Policy on Vacation Leave; Discretionary Day; Donor Leave; Bereavement Leave policy; University Policy on Disability and ADA Issues; HR Benefits (state long-term disability plan terms); FSRR Article VIII (sabbatical); Regents Policy Manual Chapter III.

Tenure-clock birth delay: KU (c8) and the Regents (c9) state the same one-year delay with slightly different cut-offs (KU: before May 1 of the year preceding the mandatory review year; Regents: before May 1 of the fifth probationary year); linked concurrent_with (V3c). The KU policy's FMLA section also states that parents with less than three months' full-time FMLA 'will be granted a one-year extension of the tenure clock in accordance with section 2' (c8).
